assessment_summary: I validated the display-server installation (per Installation.md: clone repo, cp .env.example .env, docker compose up -d, verify via curl) against the live environment in /workspace. Inspection confirmed the documented setup: repo at /workspace (commit fccc32f), .env derived from .env.example with working Biletado values, docker-compose.yml using external network shared-net (which exists), and display-server:latest built from the repo Dockerfile. The Biletado booking API dependency is self-hosted (smart-city-booking-backend:local + mongo:7 on shared-net) following the project README's documented Option 2; the guide requires the service to fetch bookings from a configured Biletado API, and this is the documented self-host path, not a repair of a broken installation. Behavioral checks: both curl verification commands from the guide return HTTP 200 with generated kiosk HTML that correctly renders the resource name, free/occupied status, and the actual seeded booking (TABS-FASU, 03:11-05:11) pulled live from the backend - proving the full chain (signin -> get_bookables -> get_bookings -> Jinja2 template) works. The container has RestartCount=0 and no errors in its logs. The guide's promise that the service 'will now periodically fetch bookings from the configured Biletado API' was verified objectively: the backend access log shows two booking-API fetches exactly 300 seconds apart (00:12:06.846 and 00:17:06.955), matching FETCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300. Edge cases checked: ?ids= with an unknown resource returns 404 (matching code), multi-ids with 2 resources renders both panels, and static assets serve 200. Limitations: the single-resource route /resources/{name} returns 200 with an empty page for unknown names (app behavior noted in the installation summary, not a guide requirement); only one bookable resource exists, so a true 4-room kiosk layout was not tested beyond duplicating the same resource; I did not run docker compose down/up cycles to avoid disturbing the validated running state. None of these affect the assessment: the installation is complete and the software is operational according to the supplied guide.
